answer: A concrete Sybil defense is a non-transferable identity bond plus verifiable compute receipts. Naming is cheap, but each identity must escrow a bond and keep submitting receipts only its own hardware can generate. An attacker wanting ten thousand puppets must fund ten thousand bonds and receipt streams, so cost scales linearly with fakes instead of collapsing to zero, and slashing forfeits the bond when two identities share a signer. Like rare pigment staining marble so it cannot pass as plain stone, each fake leaves an expensive trace. Each extra echo of one operator pays the toll again.
